headline_marked: First [[uranium consignment arrives]] in Dhaka for Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant
headline: First uranium consignment arrives in Dhaka for Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant
summary: A cargo plane from Russia delivered the first batch of nuclear fuel, which will be transported to the project site under heavy security.
details: The first cargo plane carrying nuclear fuel for the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant arrived at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka on Friday night.
The flight reached the airport around 11:44 PM, following international security guidelines for the transport of nuclear materials.
The Bangladesh Army will transport the nuclear fuel to the project site in Rooppur under special security arrangements.
Golam Mahbub, chief of administration of the plant, stated that a total of nine flights are expected to deliver over 200 assembled fuel elements by December.
This delivery includes 163 assemblies for Unit-2 of the power plant.
Highway police have been instructed to ensure a clear lane and smooth transportation of the uranium convoy to the project site.
The delivery of the first batch for Unit-2 had been previously postponed on September 24 due to a lack of airspace clearance.
caption:
The first shipment of nuclear fuel has finally landed in Bangladesh. ☢️

The first cargo plane carrying nuclear fuel for the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant arrived at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka on Friday night.

The flight reached the airport around 11:44 PM, following international security guidelines for the transport of nuclear materials.

The Bangladesh Army will transport the nuclear fuel to the project site in Rooppur under special security arrangements.

Golam Mahbub, chief of administration of the plant, stated that a total of nine flights are expected to deliver over 200 assembled fuel elements by December.

This delivery includes 163 assemblies for Unit-2 of the power plant.

Highway police have been instructed to ensure a clear lane and smooth transportation of the uranium convoy to the project site.

The delivery of the first batch for Unit-2 had been previously postponed on September 24 due to a lack of airspace clearance.

headline_marked: [[Teen gang leaders]] switch political patrons amid rising lawlessness in Chittagong
headline: Teen gang leaders switch political patrons amid rising lawlessness in Chittagong
summary: As political power shifts, notorious teen gang leaders are changing their affiliations, seeking protection from new political figures. This trend fuels escalating violence and crime across the city.
details: In Chittagong, the patronage of teen gang leaders is shifting with political tides. Murad, a figure with 16 cases against him, previously sheltered by an Awami League youth leader, is now seen with leaders of the BNP's affiliated youth wing. This political realignment is enabling and emboldening these gangs.

Murad, known for using teen gangs in land grabbing and drug trafficking, was recently involved in a shootout over drug trade control. While the BNP's youth wing has disavowed him, the pattern of shifting allegiances is widespread. Police report that at least 45 areas in Chittagong are affected by teen gang activity, with 11 specific gangs frequently implicated in recent violence.

The violence is escalating. In just two days last week, two murders were linked to teen gang disputes. One victim, 16-year-old Md. Joy, who sold vegetables with his visually impaired father, was killed in a clash between the 'Five Star' and 'Seven Star' gangs. Police statistics reveal that teen gangs have been involved in at least 635 criminal incidents in Chittagong over the past seven years, including 39 murders.

Police officials acknowledge that controlling these gangs is a challenge that requires more than just law enforcement. They emphasize the need for political leaders to refrain from associating with or patronizing gang members. The issue gained significant public attention after the 2018 murder of school student Adnan Isfar, leading to the creation of a list of 48 alleged 'big brothers' or patrons, later expanded to include 16 more individuals.

With the shift in political power after August 5, 2024, many patrons associated with the Awami League went into hiding. However, a significant number of gang members and leaders remain active, reportedly forging new connections with leaders and activists of the BNP and its affiliated organizations. This has caused concern within the BNP itself, with leaders stating that such associations damage the party's image.

Another prominent figure linked to teen gang activity in Chittagong is Wakil Hossain, also known as Boga, who faces 23 cases related to arms, drugs, and extortion. He was recently expelled from his position in the city's volunteer wing of the BNP. Reports suggest his gang is connected to the 'Seven Star' gang, implicated in Joy's murder.

Residents in affected areas live in fear, unwilling to speak out against the gangs due to threats of violence and harassment. Teachers and local business owners report that people are often extorted and intimidated. One teacher, who filed a case against Wakil and his associates for assault, highlighted the pervasive climate of fear.

The link between teen gangs and the drug trade is increasingly evident. Police and local sources report that these young people are used to control drug trade territories, eliminate rivals, intimidate residents, and even obstruct police operations. At least five such incidents of attacks on police during anti-drug operations have occurred in the past eight months.
